1 صَلَمَ , aor.
صَلِمَ , [in one of my copies of the S
صَلُمَ ,] inf. n. صَلْمٌ, (S, M, Msb, K,) He cut off, (K,) or he cut off so as to extirpate, (S, M, Msb,) a thing, (M, K, *) or an ear, (S, M, Msb, K,) and a nose; (M, K;) as also ↓ صلّم , (M, K, *) inf. n. تَصْلِيمٌ; (K;) [but] the latter verb is with teshdeed to denote muchness [of the action], or multiplicity [of the objects]: (TA:) and ↓ اِصْطَلَمَ [likewise] signifies he cut off so as to extirpate (S, * Msb, * K) a nose. (Msb.) ＝
-A2- And صَلِمَ, aor.
صَلَمَ , inf. n. صَلَمٌ, He had his ear extirpated [by amputation]. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
